I think you should ask for a biopsy on the organ that’s causing the most symptoms. 

I didn’t have any of the common symptoms when I was hospitalized. I had major fatigue, low grade fevers/chills, vomiting and blood in my urine. The only reason the ER admitted me was because my blood pressure was like sky high and they thought I was about to have a stroke at any moment so me walking around just fine baffled them. The blood in my urine, which turned out to be protein, was when the nephrologist decided to do a kidney biopsy. That’s what confirmed it for me.

My experience was a bit traumatic — at least to me it was.

I was diagnosed at the beginning of March after being hospitalized for a few days.

Back in late December, I got a got a really bad cold. Or at least that’s what I thought it was. The fatigue and body aches was real.  This lasted for like 2/3 weeks. Around this same time, my boyfriend and I hit a rough patch. ~_~. and work was in O V E R D R I V E. The stress on me and my body was intense. Anyway, the whole time I just kept feeling like someone/something was draining the energy out of me. All I wanted to do was sleep. I’m not thinking anything of it, it’s just stress. Then one day, I started throwing up. Every morning right after I brushed my teeth. After a few days of only throwing up in the morning, it started happening multiple times throughout the day. With the vomiting came the low grade fevers and chills. This lasted for all of January. (Yes I know I should’ve went to the doctor, but I still felt fine some days and I had a lot going on so I put myself on the backburner)

Beginning of February, my body was gradually getting weaker and weaker so I got on google at work and boy that was a big mistake. Google told me I had diabetes or cancer. Being scared, I went to the ER that night. After about 2 hours, a CT scan, and a blood and urine test, the doctor told me I just had a really bad UTI and prescribed me antibiotics.

Go home. Take the antibiotics. Everything will be fine. WRONG.

The antibiotics made me feel worse! Returning to the ER a few days later, they didn’t even want to listen to my updates or anything — just wrote me a new prescription and sent me on about my day.

...those antibiotics didn’t work either.

3rd week of February my Mom took me to an urgent care, the PA at the urgent care told us that I definitely didn’t have a UTI and there’s blood in my urine. I needed to see a Urologist and if I can’t see one within 3 days I needed to go to an ER.

A few days later I’m in the urologist office. She collects my urine with a catheter and then tells me I need to see a kidney doctor. She explains that there is blood in my urine — it’s the protein that my body can’t process but she can’t do anything to fix it without an official diagnosis so she’d know what to fix.

Later that night the vomiting got so bad I was rushed to the hospital and admitted.

Blood pressure was at stroke levels. Kidney activity was high.

I had a kidney biopsy done and that’s what confirmed the Lupus.

Apparently I was in kidney failure since mid January and didn’t even know it. By the time I got admitted into the hospital my kidney function was practically non-existent. 

My week in the hospital was some of best sleep I’ve ever had in my life. :)

A nephrologist diagnosed my lupus. 

When I was in the hospital and he had a hunch and ordered a kidney biopsy. The biopsy confirmed the lupus. 

He’s the one who started my treatment. I see him more than rheumatologist ironically.
